input: Coral reef bleaching occurs when corals expel the symbiotic algae (zooxanthellae) living in their tissues, causing the corals to turn white. This process is primarily triggered by increased water temperatures, often associated with climate change.  The expulsion of zooxanthellae deprives the coral of its primary food source and gives them a pale appearance. While bleached corals are not dead, they are significantly stressed and more susceptible to disease. Prolonged or severe bleaching events can lead to widespread coral mortality, devastating reef ecosystems and the biodiversity they support.  Recovery is possible if conditions improve, but repeated bleaching events hinder this process.
